context.problemStatement: Show the perpendicular legs of a right triangle with legs 3 cm and 4 cm.
context.solutionStrategy: Use the quantities given in the problem.
context.groundingProse: The 3 cm and 4 cm legs meet at a right angle. The hypotenuse is 5 cm.
context.seedNotes: Draw a right triangle and label the three lengths.

content.altText: A right triangle with a vertical leg of 3 cm, a horizontal leg of 4 cm forming a right angle, and a hypotenuse of 5 cm.

annotations.steps: I drew the two legs meeting at a 90-degree angle and connected their endpoints with the hypotenuse.
annotations.strategy: I notice that identifying the perpendicular legs first makes it easy to spot the right angle in any triangle.
annotations.misconceptions: Students sometimes mistake the longest side, or hypotenuse, for one of the perpendicular legs.
annotations.connections: This forms the foundation for using the Pythagorean theorem where the two perpendicular legs are a and b.
